significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that a model’s displacement ratio under conservation-preserving versus conservation-violating transformations, summarized by the “Conservation-Invariance Score,” inversely predicts its rate of physically inconsistent outputs across scientific laws. This establishes a broad representational phenomenon and a predictive geometric account, rather than a causal mechanism; it fixes expectations about which laws and models will fail, a consequential question given that systems such as NequIP (Batzner et al., 2022) and Equiformer (Liao and Smidt, 2023) treat physical symmetry as an explicit design constraint. True and false are distinguishable, and a negative result would specifically reject latent invariance fidelity as a general diagnostic of physical consistency, although it would not rule out other internal encodings of conserved quantities. In the topic-substitution check, the generic topic alone would not earn this score: the claim-specific coupling that “low-invariance laws predict the model’s own physically inconsistent outputs” is what raises it above the median hypothesis about merely decoding scientific concepts.

reach.justification: The named handle is the “Conservation-Invariance Score,” proposed as a “read-only diagnostic that predicts where the model produces physically inconsistent outputs,” so it is an ex-ante audit signal at the law or capability level rather than merely an explanation after an individual failure. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction survives as a relation—lower CIS should imply more downstream inconsistency—rather than leaving only a procedure for rediscovering an unconstrained direction. The hypothesis asserts scope across molecular, protein, and materials foundation models and multiple conservation laws, with downstream uptake by researchers and practitioners who audit or gate scientific models, though it does not supply an individual-example failure forecast or a demonstrated handle for scientists outside model evaluation. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic investigation of scientific representations supplies no transferable audit, whereas the quoted CIS-to-error predictive coupling supplies the required claim-specific handle and lead time.
